audience.text: Python developers who need to parse OneNote notebooks programmatically to extract pages, rich text, images, tables, attachments, tags, and numbered lists, or to generate PDF exports.

capabilities.text: Load .one files from a file path or binary stream using Document, with no external dependencies beyond Python.
capabilities.title: Parse OneNote files from path or stream

capabilities.text: Traverse pages, outlines, outline elements, rich text, images, tables, and attached files using GetChildNodes or DocumentVisitor.
capabilities.title: Traverse document tree structure

capabilities.text: Access TextRuns and TextStyle to read bold, italic, underline, hyperlinks, font, color, and paragraph styling.
capabilities.title: Extract rich text with formatting

capabilities.text: Export pages to PDF using Document.Save with SaveFormat.Pdf and PdfSaveOptions for JPEG quality and compression.
capabilities.title: Export pages to PDF

capabilities.text: Retrieve image bytes, dimensions, and file names, or attached file bytes and names for saving to disk.
capabilities.title: Extract embedded images and attachments

capabilities.text: Traverse Table, TableRow, TableCell, NoteTag, and NumberList to extract structured content and metadata.
capabilities.title: Inspect tables, tags, and numbered lists

capabilities.text: Access page revision history via PageHistory and Document.GetPageHistory().
capabilities.title: Support document revision history

limitations.text: Writing back to .one files is not implemented — this library only reads OneNote files.
Password-protected documents are not supported — supplying a password raises IncorrectPasswordException.
SaveFormat currently declares only Pdf — Document.Save raises UnsupportedSaveFormatException for any other format.
License.SetLicense() and Metered.SetMeteredKey() are no-ops in this edition and not required to use the library.
DetectLayoutChanges() is a compatibility stub and performs no layout computation.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic access to OneNote (.one) files without requiring Microsoft OneNote installation or COM automation.
Provides a pure-Python DOM for traversing OneNote document structure including pages, outlines, rich text, images, tables, and attached files.
Supports extraction of rich text with per-run formatting, hyperlinks, and paragraph styles for downstream processing.
Allows conversion of OneNote pages to PDF with configurable JPEG quality and image compression.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Note FOSS for Python is a free, open-source Python library for reading Microsoft OneNote (.one) files and exporting pages to PDF, with no dependency on Microsoft OneNote or COM automation.

uncertainties: The exact set of OneNote file versions supported beyond 'OneNote2010' is not explicitly listed beyond FileFormat enum values.
Whether PageHistory supports write operations beyond read-only inspection is not stated.
The behavior of DocumentVisitor when encountering nested or recursive node types is not detailed beyond method names.
The scope of TextStyle properties exposed (e.g., language, highlight) is listed but not their semantics.
The exact PDF rendering behavior when ASPOSE_NOTE_PDF_USE_SYSTEM_FONTS=1 is not described beyond fallback options.
Whether custom OneNote tags beyond the three predefined icons are fully supported is not clarified.
The exact behavior of RichText.Append/Insert/Replace with style arguments is not detailed.
The handling of malformed or partially corrupted .one files beyond FileCorruptedException is not specified.
